overview: The United Kingdom is an island country off the north-west coast of Europe, made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Its capital and largest city is London. The UK is a constitutional monarchy. In the 1800s and early 1900s Britain ruled the largest empire in history. It left the European Union in 2020, and it is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council.

geography.text: The UK covers the island of Great Britain, the north-east of the island of Ireland and many smaller islands. The north and west, including the Scottish Highlands and much of Wales, are hilly or mountainous, and Ben Nevis in Scotland is the highest peak. The south and east of England are lower and gentler. The UK is surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean, the North Sea, the English Channel and the Irish Sea.

history.text: England and Scotland were separate kingdoms for centuries; the Act of Union joined them as Great Britain in 1707, and Ireland was added in 1801. Britain led the Industrial Revolution and built the largest empire in history. It fought on the winning side in both World Wars, after which most of its colonies became independent. It left the European Union in 2020.

government.text: The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy. The King is head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government, which must keep the support of the House of Commons. Parliament also has an unelected House of Lords. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own parliaments or assemblies for many matters. The UK has a permanent seat with a veto on the UN Security Council.

economy.text: The UK has one of the largest economies in the world. London is a global centre for banking, finance and law, and services make up most of the economy. The UK is also strong in aerospace, medicines, cars, universities, film, music and video games. It left the European Union in 2020.

culture.text: English, the most widely learned language in the world, comes from England. The UK has given the world Shakespeare, the Beatles, Harry Potter and the BBC. Its four nations, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, each have their own traditions, from Welsh choirs to Scottish bagpipes.

items.title: Shakespeare

items.title: The Beatles
items.text: The Liverpool band became the best-selling act of all time.

items.title: Stonehenge
items.text: A prehistoric stone circle built around 5,000 years ago.

sport.text: Britain invented or first wrote down the rules of many of the world's sports, including football, rugby, cricket and tennis. England won the men's football World Cup in 1966, and Wimbledon, first played in 1877, is the oldest tennis tournament. London has hosted the Summer Olympics three times.
